messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: p99 latency spike detected for customer 'Tungsten' (vpc-dedicated pool tungsten-eu-west-1). p99 > 1500ms for last 5m, SLO(99)=500ms breached. Auto-escalation: severity=high. Paging on-call (miriam).

miriam: On it. Joining war room. Any customer-visible errors?

devin: Seeing increased tail latency on infer nodes in eu-west-1. GPU utilization 98% on pool 'tungsten-eu-west-1-dedicated'. p95 trending ~650ms, p99 ~1520ms. No obvious OOMs in logs.

jordan: FYI metrics snapshot: requests/sec for that pool spiked x3 since 11:03 UTC. KV-cache hit rate down ~12% (likely churn).

miriam: Are they in a strict isolation mode? can we route to hosted fallback? @tungsten-sre ?

tungsten-sre: Confirmed: VPC dedicated, data residency + contract prevents routing to shared hosted pool. We can accept cross-region within our reserved capacity if you coordinate.

ryan: Ok. Options: 1) scale up dedicated pool (add 2x gpus) 2) enable warm failover to eu-west-2 spare nodes in the customer reserved cluster 3) temporarily increase autoscale burst limit (their contract allows burst on approval).

ana: (support) Customer reports degraded experience in production UI, some requests hitting our retry logic. They've opened a support ticket ID #TNG-4721.

miriam: Priority: restore p99 < 500ms within 30m. Devin/Jordan, can you attempt a manual scale up and increase worker replicas? Use rictl to scale the pool.

devin: Running command now:
```
rictl scale-pool --pool tungsten-eu-west-1-dedicated --replicas 12 --type gpu-a100
```
I'll watch for scheduling.

jordan: Scheduling pods converting, but PG scheduling backlog ~40. Suspect node autoscaler slow to provision due to quota exhaustion in eu-west-1. Getting API errors: `Allocation failed: insufficient quota`.

miriam: Do we have burst capacity remaining for this customer in eu-west-1? @ryan

ryan: They have a small burst reserve of 4 GPUs but region quota is at limit for the account. Plan B: enable cross-region warm failover to eu-west-2 where they have spare capacity. That should be contract-safe.

tungsten-sre: We prefer eu-west-2 as fallback. Please confirm data egress rules—must stay within EU.

miriam: Confirmed eu-west-2 is in-region (still EU). Jordan/Devin: prepare routing change and canary 5% traffic to eu-west-2. Use `route-shift` with sticky sessions off.

devin: Preparing step:
```
rictl route-shift --customer tungsten --from eu-west-1 --to eu-west-2 --percent 5 --sticky=false
```
Will start canary in ~60s.

jordan: Before shifting, I recommend applying a quantized model fallback for long inputs to reduce per-token latency — we can do model-variant routing on a per-tenant basis. This reduces quality slightly but buys headroom.

miriam: Good call. Does contract allow model-variant fallback? (quality degradation must be communicated)

tungsten-sre: Acceptable for up to 10% of traffic while we stabilize. Notify ops.

devin: Canary started 5% to eu-west-2. Early telemetry: p99 on canary ~420ms. CPU/GPU utilization on eu-west-1 dropping ~10%.

ana: Notifying customer support to send the message about temporary quality fallback to Tungsten contacts. Draft: "We're activating cross-region failover and a temporary lower-cost model variant for a small percentage of traffic to restore latency quickly."

miriam: Great. Keep canary at 5% for 10m and monitor. If stable, ramp to 30% then 100% for a controlled failover. Jordan, keep an eye on KV-cache warmup; prefix caching may be cold in eu-west-2.

jordan: KV cache cold-start observed, hit-rate 8% initially. But model inference tail improved. I'll trigger prefix prewarm for top 50 customer prompts: `rictl cache-warm --customer tungsten --region eu-west-2 --keys-file /tmp/tungsten-top-50.txt`.

ryan: Meanwhile, I've requested quota increase with cloud provider (ticket CP-98432) and enabled temporary burst in eu-west-1 for 2 more GPUs (pending approval) — but that typically takes ~18m.

devin: Canary stable at 5m: p95 320ms, p99 450ms for canary; origin pool p99 trending down to 980ms. Rolling to 30% now.

miriam: 👍 notify customer and execs. @ana please update incident timeline and tag severity=high.

ana: Updating timeline and opening incident internal doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2178000000 (internal). Adding mitigation actions and owner assignments.

tungsten-sre: Seeing user-side latency improvements already. Thanks team. Keep us posted before ramping further.

devin: Ramp to 30% complete. p99 overall across Tungsten reduced to ~620ms. Continuing to 60% now.

jordan: Cache warm job finishing; hit rate climbing to 45% in eu-west-2. Should see further reduction in p99.

miriam: After 20m of stable metrics at 60%, we will decide on full cutover or revert. If cloud quota comes in earlier we can scale eu-west-1 instead and avoid extended cross-region.

ryan: Cloud provider approved +2 GPUs for eu-west-1 (CP-98432 resolved). If we scale eu-west-1 now, we can shift traffic back without cross-region overhead.

devin: Scaling eu-west-1 to add 2 GPUs now: `rictl add-node --region eu-west-1 --type gpu-a100 --count 2` — nodes accepted, scheduling pods.

jordan: New capacity online. Observed p99 across Tungsten now ~420ms and stable for 5m.

miriam: Great job. Start planning rollback of cross-region routing: move back to eu-west-1 in a controlled ramp. Keep 10% in eu-west-2 as warm spare for 30m then remove.

devin: Rolling back: `rictl route-shift --customer tungsten --from eu-west-2 --to eu-west-1 --percent 10` then increment.

tungsten-sre: Appreciated the clear comms and quick mitigation. We'll keep monitoring.

miriam: Incident severity will be downgraded to mitigated once p99 < 500ms for 30m. Assigning follow-ups: 1) postmortem owner: jordan 2) capacity planning + contractual burst review: ryan 3) customer comms: ana.

ana: Noted. I'll draft a short customer-facing summary and a more detailed internal postmortem template.

incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigated at 2178000365 (p99 < 500ms sustained). Please follow the postmortem playbook within 72 hours. :white_check_mark:

miriam: Closing war room in 10. Thanks everyone.
